Hence, by Lemma 5.6, and by using the lower bound ∥a∥2≥hξ\lVert a\rVert_{2}\geq h_{\xi}, we find that there exist C′,c′,n1C^{\prime},c^{\prime},n_{1} depending on ξ\xi such that for all n≥n1n\geq n_{1},

ℙ[∃u′∈ℝn−1:∥M~(−1)u′+a∥2≤2t|M~(1)]≤C′n3texp(κn)+exp(−c′n)exp(κn).\mathbb{P}[\exists u^{\prime}\in\mathbb{R}^{n-1}:\lVert\widetilde{M}^{(-1)}u^{\prime}+a\rVert_{2}\leq 2t|\widetilde{M}^{(1)}]\leq C^{\prime}n^{3}\sqrt{t}\exp(\kappa n)+\exp(-c^{\prime}n)\exp(\kappa n).

Thus, the contribution of this case is at most

∥p→∥22​n​exp⁡(2​cκ,δ′,ξ​n)​exp⁡(κ​n)​(C′​n3​t+2​exp⁡(−c′​n)).\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{2n}\exp(2c_{\kappa,\delta^{\prime},\xi}n)\exp(\kappa n)\bigg(C^{\prime}n^{3}\sqrt{t}+2\exp(-c^{\prime}n)\bigg).

By the AM-GM inequality, we have ∥p→∥22​n​t≤t​∥p→∥2n+∥p→∥23​n\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{2n}\sqrt{t}\leq t\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{n}+\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{3n}. The desired conclusion now follows by taking η>0\eta>0 sufficiently small so that ∥p→∥2n≤exp⁡(−2​η​n)\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{n}\leq\exp(-2\eta n), and then taking δ′\delta^{\prime} (hence κ\kappa) sufficiently small so that 2​cκ,δ′,ξ+κ<min⁡(c′/2,η/2)2c_{\kappa,\delta^{\prime},\xi}+\kappa<\min(c^{\prime}/2,\eta/2). ∎

The preceding proposition handles vectors in Elemi,j⁡(δ)\operatorname{Elem}_{i,j}(\delta). If the distribution ξ\xi is a translate of an origin-symmetric distribution, we also need to handle vectors in Elemi,j′⁡(δ)\operatorname{Elem}^{\prime}_{i,j}(\delta). In case the distribution ξ\xi is itself an origin-symmetric distribution, the desired bound follows immediately from the previous proposition, using that the distribution of any column of Mn​(ξ)M_{n}(\xi) is invariant under negation in this case. Therefore, it remains to handle vectors in Elemi,j′⁡(δ)\operatorname{Elem}^{\prime}_{i,j}(\delta) when ξ\xi is a nonzero translate of an origin-symmetric distribution, which is done by the next proposition.

Proposition 5.7.

Fix a discrete distribution ξ\xi that is a nonzero translate of an origin-symmetric distribution. There exist δ′,η,n0>0\delta^{\prime},\eta,n_{0}>0 depending on ξ\xi such that for all n≥n0n\geq n_{0} and t≤1t\leq 1,

ℙ[∃x∈Elem1,2′(δ′):∥Mn(ξ)x∥2≤t]≤(∥p→∥22−η)n+texp(−ηn).\mathbb{P}[\exists x\in\operatorname{Elem}_{1,2}^{\prime}(\delta^{\prime}):\lVert M_{n}(\xi)x\rVert_{2}\leq t]\leq(\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{2}-\eta)^{n}+t\exp(-\eta n).
Proof.

The proof is essentially the same as that of Proposition 5.5. The lack of the “main term” ∥p→∥22\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{2} comes from the fact that e1+e2e_{1}+e_{2} is unlikely to be a kernel vector since ξ\xi is not origin-symmetric.

We quickly discuss the main modifications to the proof of Proposition 5.5. Throughout, s≠0s\neq 0 denotes a real number such that ξ\xi and s−ξs-\xi have the same distribution (such an ss exists by our assumption about ξ\xi). First, the top-left 2×22\times 2 minor of QQ is now

[12−121212].\begin{bmatrix}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}&-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}&\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{bmatrix}.

Next, we let Ξ=supp⁡(ξ+ξ′)/2\Xi=\operatorname{supp}(\xi+\xi^{\prime})/\sqrt{2} and as before, let

𝒞:={a∈Ξn:∃λ∈ℝ​ with ​∥a−λ​1n∥2≤8​K​δ′​n}\mathcal{C}:=\{a\in\Xi^{n}:\exists\lambda\in\mathbb{R}\text{ with }\lVert a-\lambda 1_{n}\rVert_{2}\leq 8K\delta^{\prime}\sqrt{n}\}

and for z∈Ξz\in\Xi,

𝒞z:=𝒞∩{a∈ℝn:|supp⁡(a−z​1n)|≤κ​n},\mathcal{C}_{z}:=\mathcal{C}\cap\{a\in\mathbb{R}^{n}:|\operatorname{supp}(a-z1_{n})|\leq\kappa n\},

where κ=κ⁡(δ′,ξ)>0\kappa=\kappa(\delta^{\prime},\xi)>0 is chosen as in the previous argument. For such a choice of κ\kappa, we have

ℙ[M~(1)∈𝒞]≤∥p→∥22​nexp(2cκ,δ′,ξn), and \mathbb{P}[\widetilde{M}^{(1)}\in\mathcal{C}]\leq\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{2n}\exp(2c_{\kappa,\delta^{\prime},\xi}n),\text{ and }
ℙ[M~(1)∈𝒞∖𝒞s/2]≤(∥p→∥22−cξ)n.\mathbb{P}[\widetilde{M}^{(1)}\in\mathcal{C}\setminus\mathcal{C}_{s/\sqrt{2}}]\leq(\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{2}-c_{\xi})^{n}.

This time the inequalities are derived as follows. We note that, by Cauchy-Schwarz, for any z∈Ξz\in\Xi, ℙ[ξ+ξ′=z2]≤∥p→∥22\mathbb{P}[\xi+\xi^{\prime}=z\sqrt{2}]\leq\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{2}, with equality holding if and only if ℙ[ξ=a]=ℙ[ξ′=z2−a]\mathbb{P}[\xi=a]=\mathbb{P}[\xi^{\prime}=z\sqrt{2}-a] for all a∈supp⁡(ξ)a\in\operatorname{supp}(\xi), which happens if and only if z=s/2z=s/\sqrt{2}.

Using this, we have as before that

ℙ[ℰ]≤∥p→∥23​n+(∥p→∥22−cξ)n+∑a∈𝒞s/2ℙ[M~(1)=a]ℙ[∃u′∈ℝn−1:∥M~(−1)u′+a∥2≤2t|M~(1)].\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}]\leq\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{3n}+(\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{2}-c_{\xi})^{n}+\sum_{a\in\mathcal{C}_{s/\sqrt{2}}}\mathbb{P}[\widetilde{M}^{(1)}=a]\mathbb{P}[\exists u^{\prime}\in\mathbb{R}^{n-1}:\lVert\widetilde{M}^{(-1)}u^{\prime}+a\rVert_{2}\leq 2t|\widetilde{M}^{(1)}].

The most important detail is that for κ≤1/2\kappa\leq 1/2 (say), every a∈𝒞s/2a\in\mathcal{C}_{s/\sqrt{2}} is nonzero, since it has at least (1−κ)​n(1-\kappa)n coordinates equal to s/2s/\sqrt{2}. Since ss is a nonzero constant depending only on ξ\xi, we can now use the analysis in Case II of the proof of Proposition 5.5. The final thing to note is that the distribution of the random variable (ξ−ξ′)/2(\xi-\xi^{\prime})/\sqrt{2}, conditioned on (ξ+ξ′)/2=s/2(\xi+\xi^{\prime})/\sqrt{2}=s/\sqrt{2} coincides with the distribution of (2​ξ∗−s)/2(2\xi^{\ast}-s)/\sqrt{2}, where ξ∗\xi^{\ast} has the same support as ξ\xi, but takes on atom aia_{i} with probability proportional to pi2p_{i}^{2}. The remaining details of the proof are essentially the same. ∎

5.2. One column

We now handle vectors in Elemi⁡(δ′)\operatorname{Elem}_{i}(\delta^{\prime}). Once again, by permutation invariance, it suffices to handle Elem1⁡(δ′)\operatorname{Elem}_{1}(\delta^{\prime}). We will prove the following.

Proposition 5.8.

Fix a discrete distribution ξ\xi. There exist C′,δ′,η,n0>0C^{\prime},\delta^{\prime},\eta,n_{0}>0 depending on ξ\xi such that for all n≥n0n\geq n_{0} and t≤1t\leq 1,

ℙ[∃x∈Elem1(δ′):∥Mn(ξ)x∥2≤t]≤p0n+C′texp(−ηn)+(∥p→∥22−η)n.\mathbb{P}[\exists x\in\operatorname{Elem}_{1}(\delta^{\prime}):\lVert M_{n}(\xi)x\rVert_{2}\leq t]\leq p_{0}^{n}+C^{\prime}t\exp(-\eta n)+(\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{2}-\eta)^{n}.

The analysis is more delicate than the two column case, since (i) we may have p0<∥p→∥∞p_{0}<\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{\infty}, but we still want to isolate p0p_{0} as the major contribution coming from these events, and (ii) we are aiming for an error term of (∥p→∥22−η)n(\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{2}-\eta)^{n}, which may be smaller than (p0−η)n(p_{0}-\eta)^{n}. However, given the preparation above, the rest of the proof is similar to the proof in the sparse Bernoulli case, isolated in [7, Proposition 2.8], except that we need to replace the application of the results of Rudelson and Vershynin [19] with the much sharper Proposition 4.4 and Theorem 4.5.

We begin with the following proposition. The analogue in the sparse Bernoulli case is [7, Lemma 2.9].

Lemma 5.9.

Fix a discrete distribution ξ\xi. For any η∈(0,1)\eta\in(0,1), there exist C,n0>0C,n_{0}>0 depending on ξ,η\xi,\eta for which the following holds. For any v∈ℝnv\in\mathbb{R}^{n} with ∥v∥2≥1\lVert v\rVert_{2}\geq 1, we have

ℙ[∃x∈ℝn−1:∥Ax−v∥2≤t]≤C⋅n3t1/2+(∥p→∥∞+η)n,\mathbb{P}[\exists x\in\mathbb{R}^{n-1}:\lVert Ax-v\rVert_{2}\leq t]\leq C\cdot n^{3}t^{1/2}+(\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{\infty}+\eta)^{n},

where AA is a random n×(n−1)n\times(n-1) matrix with independent ξ\xi entries.

Proof.

Fix η>0\eta>0, and let ℰ\mathcal{E} be the event whose probability we are trying to control. After potentially reindexing the coordinates, we may write

A=[RAn−1],v=[v1v′]A=\begin{bmatrix}R\\ A_{n-1}\end{bmatrix},\quad v=\begin{bmatrix}v_{1}\\ v^{\prime}\end{bmatrix}

where An−1A_{n-1} is an (n−1)×(n−1)(n-1)\times(n-1) matrix and v′∈ℝn−1v^{\prime}\in\mathbb{R}^{n-1} satisfies ∥v′∥2≥1/2\lVert v^{\prime}\rVert_{2}\geq 1/2. Let ℰS={sn−1(An−1)≤t}\mathcal{E}_{S}=\{s_{n-1}(A_{n-1})\leq\sqrt{t}\}. By Theorem 4.5, we have that for all sufficiently large nn, there exists a constant C′C^{\prime} depending on ξ\xi and η\eta such that

ℙ⁡[ℰS]≤C′​n​t+(∥p→∥∞+η/2)n.\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}_{S}]\leq C^{\prime}\sqrt{nt}+(\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{\infty}+\eta/2)^{n}.

It therefore suffices to bound the probability of ℰ∧ℰSc\mathcal{E}\wedge\mathcal{E}_{S}^{c}. In such a situation, we see that y:=(An−1)−1​v′y:=(A_{n-1})^{-1}v^{\prime} is unique. Let y0:=y/∥y∥2y_{0}:=y/\lVert y\rVert_{2}, and for δ,ρ,L\delta,\rho,L to be chosen momentarily, let

ℰU={y0∈Cons(δ,ρ)∨𝒯ξ(y0,L)≥(∥p→∥∞+η/2)n}.\mathcal{E}_{U}=\{y_{0}\in\operatorname{Cons}(\delta,\rho)\vee\mathcal{T}_{\xi}(y_{0},L)\geq(\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{\infty}+\eta/2)^{n}\}.

By Proposition 4.4, we can choose δ,ρ,L>0\delta,\rho,L>0 depending on ξ\xi and η\eta so that

ℙ⁡[ℰU]≤(∥p→∥∞+η/2)n.\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}_{U}]\leq(\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{\infty}+\eta/2)^{n}.

Hence, it suffices to bound the probability of ℰ∧ℰSc∧ℰUc\mathcal{E}\wedge\mathcal{E}_{S}^{c}\wedge\mathcal{E}_{U}^{c}. Let x∈ℝn−1x\in\mathbb{R}^{n-1} be a vector certifying this event. Then, we have for all sufficiently large nn that

∥An−1​x−v′∥2≤t⟹∥x−y∥2≤t1/2, and \lVert A_{n-1}x-v^{\prime}\rVert_{2}\leq t\implies\lVert x-y\rVert_{2}\leq t^{1/2},\text{ and }
|R​x−v1|≤t⟹|R​y−v1|≤t+n​t1/2.|Rx-v_{1}|\leq t\implies|Ry-v_{1}|\leq t+nt^{1/2}.

Furthermore, since ∥v∥2≥1\lVert v\rVert_{2}\geq 1, we have ∥y∥2≥1/C′′​n2\lVert y\rVert_{2}\geq 1/C^{\prime\prime}n^{2}, for some constant C′′C^{\prime\prime} depending on ξ\xi.

We now fix a realization of An−1A_{n-1} satisfying ℰSc∧ℰUc\mathcal{E}_{S}^{c}\wedge\mathcal{E}_{U}^{c}. In particular, this fixes y,y0y,y_{0} satisfying the conditions in ℰUc\mathcal{E}_{U}^{c} and with ∥y∥2≥1/C′′​n2\lVert y\rVert_{2}\geq 1/C^{\prime\prime}n^{2}. Now, we use the independence of RR and An−1A_{n-1} and the fact that ℰ\mathcal{E} implies

|R​y−v1|≤t+n​t1/2≤2​n​t1/2.|Ry-v_{1}|\leq t+nt^{1/2}\leq 2nt^{1/2}.

Since

𝒯ξ​(y0,L)<(∥p→∥∞+η/2)n\mathcal{T}_{\xi}(y_{0},L)<(\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{\infty}+\eta/2)^{n}

and ∥y∥2≥1/C′′​n2\lVert y\rVert_{2}\geq 1/C^{\prime\prime}n^{2}, we find that the desired probability is bounded by

2​L​C′′​n3​t1/2+L​(∥p→∥∞+η/2)n.∎2LC^{\prime\prime}n^{3}t^{1/2}+L(\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{\infty}+\eta/2)^{n}.\qed

Now we are ready to conclude Proposition 5.8.

Proof of Proposition 5.8.

A completely identical argument to the proof of Proposition 5.5 shows that for a sufficiently large constant KK depending on ξ\xi, and for Ξ:=supp⁡(ξ)⊆ℝ\Xi:=\operatorname{supp(\xi)}\subseteq\mathbb{R},

ℙ[ℰ]≤p03​n+∑a∈𝒞ℙ[M(1)=a]ℙ[∃u′∈ℝn−1:∥M(−1)u′+a∥2≤2t],\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}]\leq p_{0}^{3n}+\sum_{a\in\mathcal{C}}\mathbb{P}[M^{(1)}=a]\mathbb{P}[\exists u^{\prime}\in\mathbb{R}^{n-1}:\lVert M^{(-1)}u^{\prime}+a\rVert_{2}\leq 2t],

where M(1)M^{(1)} denotes the first column of MnM_{n}, M(−1)M^{(-1)} denotes the n×(n−1)n\times(n-1) matrix formed by excluding this column, and

𝒞={a∈Ξn:∃λ∈ℝ​ with ​∥a−λ​1n∥2≤8​K​δ′​n}.\mathcal{C}=\{a\in\Xi^{n}:\exists\lambda\in\mathbb{R}\text{ with }\lVert a-\lambda 1_{n}\rVert_{2}\leq 8K\delta^{\prime}\sqrt{n}\}.

We want to bound the contribution of the sum on the right hand side.

Case I: If a=0a=0, ℙ[M(1)=a]=p0n\mathbb{P}[M^{(1)}=a]=p_{0}^{n}.

Case II: If a≠0a\neq 0, then ∥a∥2≥hξ>0\lVert a\rVert_{2}\geq h_{\xi}>0. Hence, by Lemma 5.9, there is a constant C>0C>0 depending on ξ,η\xi,\eta such that

ℙ[∃u′∈ℝn−1:∥M(−1)u′+a∥2≤2t]≤Cn3t+(∥p→∥∞+η/2)n.\mathbb{P}[\exists u^{\prime}\in\mathbb{R}^{n-1}:\lVert M^{(-1)}u^{\prime}+a\rVert_{2}\leq 2t]\leq Cn^{3}\sqrt{t}+(\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{\infty}+\eta/2)^{n}.

Moreover, a similar (but easier) argument as in the proof of Proposition 5.5 shows that

ℙ[M(1)∈𝒞]≤∥p→∥∞nexp(cξ,δ′n),\mathbb{P}[M^{(1)}\in\mathcal{C}]\leq\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{\infty}^{n}\exp(c_{\xi,\delta^{\prime}}n),

where cξ,δ′c_{\xi,\delta^{\prime}} goes to 00 as δ′\delta^{\prime} goes to 00.

Hence, we see that the contribution to the sum from this case is bounded by

∥p→∥∞n​exp⁡(cξ,δ′​n)⋅(C​n3​t+(∥p→∥∞+η/2)n).\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{\infty}^{n}\exp(c_{\xi,\delta^{\prime}}n)\cdot\bigg(Cn^{3}\sqrt{t}+(\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{\infty}+\eta/2)^{n}\bigg).

By choosing δ′\delta^{\prime} sufficiently small depending on ξ\xi and η\eta, and using ∥p→∥∞2≤∥p→∥22−cξ\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{\infty}^{2}\leq\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{2}-c_{\xi} for some cξ>0c_{\xi}>0, we see as before (using the AM-GM inequality) that the above quantity is at most

t​exp⁡(−η′​n)+(∥p→∥22−η′)nt\exp(-\eta^{\prime}n)+(\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{2}-\eta^{\prime})^{n}

for a sufficiently small η′\eta^{\prime} depending on ξ\xi and η\eta. This completes the proof. ∎

The proof of Theorem 1.5 is now immediate.

Proof of Theorem 1.5.

First, assume that ξ\xi is not a shift of an origin-symmetric random variable. We choose δ′\delta^{\prime} small enough so that the conclusions of Propositions 5.8 and 5.5 are satisfied. By the union bound, this shows that the contribution of Elem⁡(δ′)\operatorname{Elem}(\delta^{\prime}) to the probability is at most

n​ℙ​[ℰe1]+(n2)​ℙ​[ℰe1−e2]+(t+∥p→∥22​n)​e−η​n,n\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}_{e_{1}}]+\binom{n}{2}\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}_{e_{1}-e_{2}}]+(t+\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{2n})e^{-\eta n},

for a sufficiently small η>0\eta>0 depending on ξ\xi, and for all sufficiently large nn depending on ξ\xi. Now, we can conclude using Corollary 5.4.

Next, if ξ\xi is a nonzero shift of an origin-symmetric random variable, we do the same, except we require Propositions 5.8, 5.5, and 5.7 and then conclude with Corollary 5.4.

Finally, we consider the case when ξ\xi is an origin-symmetric random variable. As before, we begin by using Propositions 5.8 and 5.5. The only thing to note is that, by the symmetry of ξ\xi about the origin, for all i≠ji\neq j, ℙ⁡[ℰei−ej]=ℙ⁡[ℰei+ej]\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}_{e_{i}-e_{j}}]=\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}_{e_{i}+e_{j}}]. Hence, by the union bound, the contribution of Elem′⁡(δ′)\operatorname{Elem}^{\prime}(\delta^{\prime}) to the probability is at most

n​ℙ​[ℰe1]+(n2)⁡(ℙ⁡[ℰe1−e2]+ℙ⁡[ℰe1+e2])+(t+∥p→∥22​n)​e−η​n.n\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}_{e_{1}}]+\binom{n}{2}(\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}_{e_{1}-e_{2}}]+\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}_{e_{1}+e_{2}}])+(t+\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{2n})e^{-\eta n}.

Now, we can conclude using Corollary 5.4. ∎

6. Deduction of Theorems 1.4 and 1.2

Given the results in Sections 3 and 5, the deduction of Theorems 1.4 and 1.2 is immediate. Fix a discrete distribution ξ\xi, and let δ,ρ,η,n0>0\delta,\rho,\eta,n_{0}>0 be parameters depending on ξ\xi coming from Theorem 1.5. Then, for the proof of Theorem 1.4, let ϵ>0\epsilon>0 be as in the statement of the theorem (it suffices to assume that ϵ<1\epsilon<1), and for the proof of Theorem 1.2, let ϵ>0\epsilon>0 be such that

exp⁡(2​ϵ−H⁡(p→))<∥p→∥22,\exp(2\epsilon-H(\vec{p}))<\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{2},

which is possible since, by the weighted AM-GM inequality, we have

exp⁡(−H⁡(p→))=∏ipipi≤∑ipi2=∥p→∥22,\exp(-H(\vec{p}))=\prod_{i}p_{i}^{p_{i}}\leq\sum_{i}p_{i}^{2}=\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{2},

and equality holds if and only if ξ\xi is uniform on its support.

Let C=C3.8​(ξ,δ,ρ,ϵ/2)C=C_{\ref{thm:incompressible}}(\xi,\delta,\rho,\epsilon/2). By taking Cξ,ϵC_{\xi,\epsilon} in Theorem 1.4 and CξC_{\xi} in Theorem 1.2 to be at least CC, we may restrict our attention to 0≤t≤1/C0\leq t\leq 1/C (since for t≥1/Ct\geq 1/C, the right-hand sides of Theorems 1.4 and 1.2 are at least 11). By Theorem 1.5 and Theorem 3.8, for all 0≤t≤1/C0\leq t\leq 1/C, we have

ℙ[sn(Mn(ξ))≤t/n]\displaystyle\mathbb{P}[s_{n}(M_{n}(\xi))\leq t/\sqrt{n}] ≤ℙ[infx∈Cons⁡(δ,ρ)∥Mn(ξ)x∥2≤t/n]+ℙ[infy∈Cons⁡(δ,ρ)∥yMn(ξ)∥2≤Ct]\displaystyle\leq\mathbb{P}\bigg[\inf_{x\in\operatorname{Cons}(\delta,\rho)}\lVert M_{n}(\xi)x\rVert_{2}\leq t/\sqrt{n}\bigg]+\mathbb{P}\bigg[\inf_{y\in\operatorname{Cons}(\delta,\rho)}\lVert yM_{n}(\xi)\rVert_{2}\leq Ct\bigg]
+ℙ[infx∈Noncons⁡(δ,ρ)∥Mn(ξ)x∥2≤t/n∧infy∈Cons⁡(δ,ρ)∥yMn(ξ)∥2>Ct]\displaystyle\quad+\mathbb{P}\bigg[\inf_{x\in\operatorname{Noncons}(\delta,\rho)}\lVert M_{n}(\xi)x\rVert_{2}\leq t/\sqrt{n}\wedge\inf_{y\in\operatorname{Cons}(\delta,\rho)}\lVert yM_{n}(\xi)\rVert_{2}>Ct\bigg]
≤2​n​ℙ​[ℰe1]+(n2−n)​(ℙ⁡[ℰe1−e2]+ℙ⁡[ℰe1+e2])+2​(C​t+∥p→∥22​n)​e−η​n\displaystyle\leq 2n\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}_{e_{1}}]+(n^{2}-n)(\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}_{e_{1}-e_{2}}]+\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}_{e_{1}+e_{2}}])+2(Ct+\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{2n})e^{-\eta n}
+C​t+exp⁡((ϵ/2−H⁡(p→))​n)\displaystyle\quad+Ct+\exp((\epsilon/2-H(\vec{p}))n)

for all sufficiently large nn. Here, we have used that Mn​(ξ)M_{n}(\xi) and Mn​(ξ)⊺M_{n}(\xi)^{\intercal} have the same distribution.

For Theorem 1.2, we are done by our choice of ϵ\epsilon.

For Theorem 1.4, we note that by Cauchy-Schwarz (as in Proposition 5.2), ℙ⁡[ℰe1+e2]≤ℙ⁡[ℰe1−e2]\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}_{e_{1}+e_{2}}]\leq\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}_{e_{1}-e_{2}}] and recall from above that exp⁡(−H⁡(p→))≤∥p→∥22\exp(-H(\vec{p}))\leq\lVert\vec{p}\rVert_{2}^{2}. Using this, we can bound the right hand side of the above computation by

2​C​t+2​n​ℙ​[ℰe1]+2​n2​exp⁡(ϵ​n/2)​ℙ​[ℰe1−e2].2Ct+2n\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}_{e_{1}}]+2n^{2}\exp(\epsilon n/2)\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{E}_{e_{1}-e_{2}}].

The desired conclusion follows since 2​n2​exp⁡(ϵ​n/2)≤(1+ϵ)n2n^{2}\exp(\epsilon n/2)\leq(1+\epsilon)^{n} for all ϵ<1\epsilon<1 and nn sufficiently large.
